skill.name: analyzing-component-quality
skill.description: Analyzes Claude Code agents, skills, commands, and hooks for component quality. Scores clarity, tool permissions, trigger design, security posture, and usability, then suggests concrete improvements.
skill.summary: Evaluate Claude Code component quality with scoring rubrics and improvement guidance.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick and reconnaissance matches are false positives caused by Markdown examples, code fences, and checklist text. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious command execution was found, but the skill does declare broad Bash access for an analysis workflow.

remediation.issue: Bash is granted in the skill frontmatter for a mostly read-only quality review workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools unless running the helper script is required. If kept, document exact commands and validate component paths.

remediation.issue: The documentation names helper scripts that are not included in the package.
remediation.suggestion: Either add the missing helper scripts or remove those references so users do not run unexpected alternatives.

static_findings.snippet: **4.0 - Good**: Solid component, some enhancements recommended
- `Bash, Write, Edit` - Command injection + file access
- Does it have appropriate `{baseDir}` usage for resources?
**Current**: `allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task`
**Current**: `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task`
- **Quality ≠ Correctness**: Valid components can still be low quality

semantic_findings.title: Broad Bash Permission for Analysis Skill
semantic_findings.description: The skill frontmatter grants Bash access although most review steps are read-only analysis. The documentation also shows optional Python helper execution, so users should treat it as shell-capable.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The frontmatter directly declares Bash, and the documented workflow includes running a local Python helper. No malicious command is present, so the risk is broad shell capability rather than confirmed abuse.

content.value_statement: Claude Code components can pass validation but still be unclear, over-permissioned, or hard to use. This skill applies a quality rubric and produces targeted improvement guidance for marketplace readiness.
actual_capabilities: Scores description clarity, tool permissions, triggers, security, and usability on a 1 to 5 scale.
Reviews agents, skills, commands, and hooks using documented quality standards.
Identifies excessive tools, vague descriptions, unclear triggers, and weak usability patterns.
Provides before-and-after improvement suggestions for component documentation and permissions.
Includes a local quality-scorer.py helper for heuristic analysis of Markdown components.
limitations: Assumes the component already passed technical validation and schema checks.
The included helper script does not implement hook analysis.
Only quality-scorer.py is included; two helper scripts named in the docs are not present.
Quality scores are heuristic and should be reviewed by a human before publishing.

use_cases.title: Review a New Skill Before Publishing
use_cases.description: Assess description clarity, triggers, permissions, security, and usability before listing a skill in a marketplace.

use_cases.title: Improve an Agent Definition
use_cases.description: Find unclear invocation criteria, unnecessary tools, and weak examples in an agent Markdown file.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Component Reviews
use_cases.description: Use the same quality dimensions across internal skills, commands, agents, and hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Component Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one component file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Claude Code component for quality. Score each dimension and list the most important improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Permission Focus Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review focused on tool access.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for tool permission quality. Explain which tools are justified and which should be removed.

prompt_templates.title: Marketplace Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this component against marketplace standards. Include quality scores, security concerns, usability gaps, and publish readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Full Improvement Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rewrite guidance for a weak component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized improvement plan for this component. Include revised descriptions, trigger wording, permissions, and documentation changes.

output_examples.input: A skill has a vague description and broad tool permissions.
output_examples.output: The report rates description clarity as poor, flags excessive tools, and recommends a specific trigger-focused description.

output_examples.input: An agent includes Task without a clear orchestration role.
output_examples.output: The report identifies circular delegation risk and suggests removing Task or converting the agent into a skill.

output_examples.input: A marketplace reviewer needs a final publish decision.
output_examples.output: The report summarizes strengths, blockers, recommended fixes, and the expected quality score after changes.

best_practices: Run the review on components that already pass schema and frontmatter validation.
Compare each finding with the included quality standards before accepting the recommendation.
Treat Bash or write-capable permissions as needing clear justification and path validation.
anti_patterns: Do not use the score as the only approval signal for marketplace publication.
Do not ignore missing helper scripts or undocumented workflow steps.
Do not keep broad tool permissions only because examples mention them.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes Claude Code components for clarity, permissions, triggers, security posture, and usability.

faq.question: Does it validate component schemas?
faq.answer: No. It assumes schema validation already passed and focuses on quality and effectiveness.

faq.question: Can it review agents and skills?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation covers agents, skills, commands, and hooks, with strongest support for Markdown components.

faq.question: Does it include an automated tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes quality-scorer.py for heuristic scoring of component Markdown files.

faq.question: Is Bash access required?
faq.answer: Bash is only useful for running the local helper script. Read-only reviews can be done without Bash.

faq.question: Can Codex use this workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can follow the rubric to review Claude Code components and produce improvement guidance.
